next.mintHint: Paste the key when the first line waits, then press Enter; it never appears on a command line. The commands list the key's knowledge bases, then mint a token for the one whose id you set as KB_ID. The permissions must be within that knowledge base's "capabilities" in the list; lower them for one you can only read. Change the name and tools as you need. The reply shows the token once. If it is lost, rerunning the last command with the same MINT_KEY names the token but can't show its secret: revoke that token and mint again with a new MINT_KEY.
next.checkHint: Paste the key when the first line waits, then press Enter; it never appears on a command line. The reply says what the key may do.
next.mintCreatedHint: Paste the key when the first line waits, then press Enter; it never appears on a command line. This key reaches only knowledge bases it creates, so the commands create one first, then mint a token for it (set KB_ID from the reply). The reply shows the token once. If it is lost, rerunning the last command with the same MINT_KEY names the token but can't show its secret: revoke that token and mint again with a new MINT_KEY.

cli.title: Command line (kb)
cli.description: Connect another computer to this server: run the command below on it. It installs the kb release that matches this server, checks it against the release's checksums, then prints a sign-in link. Open the link, sign in and approve the device to log it in.
cli.copyUnix: Copy the Linux and macOS install command
cli.hint: kb is installed in ~/.cargo/bin (%USERPROFILE%\.cargo\bin on Windows). An approved device appears under Personal access tokens, where you can revoke it.

connect.title: Connect an AI client
connect.description: Add this server to Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client. The client signs in with your account in the browser, so there's no secret to copy.

oauth.claude: Then run /mcp in Claude Code, pick {{name}} and choose Authenticate. Approve the access in your browser. Add --scope user to use it in every project.
oauth.codex: The login opens your browser; approve the access there.
oauth.other: Add this to the client's MCP settings, or paste the server URL where it asks for one. It opens your browser to sign in; approve the access there.

token.claude: Paste the token when the first line waits, then press Enter. Claude Code reads {{env}} from the environment it starts in, so set it there in later sessions too (from a secret manager or your shell profile). The token stays out of your shell history and Claude Code's settings.
token.codex: Paste the token when the first line waits, then press Enter. Codex reads {{env}} from the shell that starts it, so set it there in later sessions too (from a secret manager or your shell profile).
token.other: For a client's private settings file only: it contains the token. Never commit or share it.

connect.protocol: Clients must speak MCP {{version}} over Streamable HTTP. Current Claude Code and Codex do; an older client gets "Unsupported protocol version".
